description: Rulings on the S&P 500 panel on securities' total returns where a distribution of another company's shares -- a spin-off -- is not carried, or carried wrongly, by the cache's records. Rulings, not vendor data, so in the repo rather than in data/, as the count rulings are carried. Each entry: the parent's key, label and name; the child's ticker and composite FIGI; the ratio, the child's shares a parent share; the record, distribution and ex-dates; 'split', a split the parent made with the distribution that the cache does not record, applied to its count; 'child_count' 'parent', a child whose records carry no count seeded with the parent's on the record date at the ratio until Polygon carries one, and 'retained' the share of the child the parent kept, the seeded count the shares distributed over the rest (midoffice15); 'supersedes', count overrides this ruling replaces; the evidence; and 'held', a ruling held until it is understood, with why -- read and listed by the build, never applied (midoffice15). On the ex-date the build sets the parent's total return to (w (C_t + D_t) + k V) / C_s - 1, C its raw closes that day and the priced day before, D its cash that day, V the child's close that day -- or its first after, where it had none -- and w the splits it applies between; the stitched prices are left as Polygon has them. Read by scripts/build_sp500_securities.py, which lists every ruling it applies (midoffice14).

entries.held: The record: S&P Global's release of 2026-05-21 -- two ways to trade SPGI from about 06-26 through 06-30, regular-way with the entitlement and SPGI WI without it -- so 07-01 is the first day SPGI trades without it, the ruled ex-date; unlike Lennar's, the record date is not the ex-date. The data show no gap of Mobility's size on either day. On the record date SPGI opened -0.16% and closed +1.23% against its peers' median -0.09% and +0.54% (MCO, MSCI, ICE, CME, NDAQ, FDS), and the day after +1.39% and +2.16% against +0.82% and +0.11%. On 07-01, Mobility worth 4.98% of SPGI's prior close at its first open and 5.20% at its first close, SPGI opened -1.89% against its peers' +0.74% -- -2.63 points, about half the distribution, the largest such gap from 06-02 to 07-10 (the next -0.80) -- and closed +1.89% against +4.27%; over 07-01 and 07-02 together its raw return, +8.01%, is its peers' (+7.14% to +8.70%, median +7.86%) without the distribution, and +13.53% with it. Neither the record date nor the ex-date shows the distribution in SPGI's raw prices, so the ruling is held until it is understood -- by an outside price for SPGI's regular-way close of 2026-06-30, say; the panel keeps Polygon's +1.89% on 07-01 meanwhile.
